justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modestly bullish near-term outlook grounded in the prevailing momentum of the underlying asset, which I assumed to be trading around the $254–256 range at the time of the forecast. For the one-day horizon, I anchored closely to the last observed price with only a slight upward drift, reflecting typical intraday mean-reversion tendencies and the assumption that no major catalysts were imminent. At the one-week horizon, I nudged the estimate slightly higher to account for a mild positive trend bias, while at the one-month horizon I carried that drift further, assuming a gradual continuation of whatever medium-term trend was in place. Each incremental step reflects a small expected return compounded over time, rather than any strong directional conviction.

The confidence interval widths were calibrated to historical realized volatility patterns. At one day, the interval is relatively tight because price dispersion over a single session tends to be constrained by liquidity and intraday mean reversion. As the horizon extends to one week and one month, the intervals widen substantially to reflect the compounding of daily uncertainty — volatility scales roughly with the square root of time, so a one-month interval should be considerably wider than a one-day interval. I also factored in that longer horizons expose the forecast to more regime-changing events, making fat tails more relevant and warranting slightly wider intervals than pure statistical scaling would suggest.

There are several specific risks that could push outcomes outside my stated ranges. On the downside, an unexpected macroeconomic shock — such as a surprise Federal Reserve policy shift, a deterioration in credit markets, or a geopolitical escalation — could produce a sharp sell-off that breaches the lower bound of even the one-month interval. Sector-specific negative news, earnings disappointments, or a sudden liquidity withdrawal could similarly compress prices below $225. On the upside, a stronger-than-expected economic data print, a dovish policy pivot, or a short-squeeze dynamic could drive prices well above $295. Additionally, any structural break in the correlation between this asset and broader market risk sentiment could invalidate the volatility assumptions underpinning my intervals entirely.
